verdict.rationale: Obsidian's docs state that notes are non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files stored locally, readable and editable with other text editors, and usable offline. Community users independently confirm they own their files as plain text that can outlive the app. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of which features work fully offline, beyond the general statement that Obsidian can be used offline.

support.subject: As a power-user, my notes live in local files or a local-first store that I own and can read without the app, and everything keeps working fully offline

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline and switch to another app easily
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
Obsidian stores your notes as Markdown-formatted plain text files in a vault.
as plain text they can outlive Obsidian itself
